text:
kate: Heads-up: prod wants to add a hard candidate limit on /v2/rerank. Two quick asks: 1) what's the canonical score field we return (normalized vs raw)? 2) how should routing/quotas behave when candidate_count is large?

srinivas: +1 on canonicalization. My default: return a single top-level `score` normalized to 0..1 for callers that only care about rank. Put `raw_score` optional for internal models. Backwards compat: keep `score` name but add `score_type` enum so clients can detect.

elaine: telemetry needs to capture `candidate_count`, `model_variant`, `time_to_first_score`, `p50/p95_lat` and whether a fallback model was used. Dashboard: additive hist for candidate_count and a scatter of latency vs candidate_count.

tilly: from product: console UX should let customers set a soft default candidate_limit per-route and a hard maximum at org level. Also we want an alert when >5% of requests hit the hard limit.

srinivas: for quotas, I propose unit = "score_unit" where 1 scored candidate = 1 unit. That maps well to cost/throughput. For routing: if a request exceeds dedicated pool QPS or unit budget, fallback to cheaper model or enqueue (if caller sets wait=true).

kate: sounds good. Need clarity on limits: suggest default per-request candidate_limit=200, soft warn at 500, hard cap 2000. These numbers are tunable per-tenant. Also think about KV cache impact: scoring many candidates with long context can explode KV usage.

elaine: +KV note. Telemetry should also record `avg_context_len` and estimated KV cache hits to attribute cost properly.

opsbot: deploy-bot: "staging:rerank-contract-tests" started by srinivas at 1965341400

srinivas: quick compatibility note: older clients expect descending scores (higher==better). We should document `sort_order` in response envelope and include `scores_ascending: false` default.

kate: agreed. Also introduce a compact mode for high-volume customers: return only ids + score (no metadata) to reduce payload. We'll surface `response_profile=compact|full` param.

elaine: dashboard UX: add per-route heatmap of `candidate_count` vs `model_variant` so ops can see which models get the heavy fanout. Add alert rule templates for costly routes.

tilly: rollout plan: canary new contract for 10% of orgs with autosanitized guidance: if any canary tenant sees >2x cost we rollback. Need an experiment metric: "cost_per_1000_requests"

kate: for API schema, propose this minimal response shape (stability-first):

```json
{
  "scores_ascending": false,
  "model": "rerank-3b-v2",
  "response_profile": "full",
  "results": [
    {"id": "c123", "score": 0.87, "raw_score": 234.5, "meta": {...}},
    {"id": "c234", "score": 0.83}
  ]
}
```

kate: keep that `meta` optional and allow `results` to be streamed.

elaine: streaming wise, telemetry must emit an event at the end with `final_candidate_count` and `streaming_duration` so we can tie billing.

tilly: one more product ask: allow per-route `model_affinity` hints so console can show "preferred" cheaper models in UI and let ops override.

opsbot: infra-bot: note recorded - added ticket INF-827 to track quota unit implementation.

kate: action items: 1) srinivas - draft API schema + compatibility notes, 2) elaine - telemetry/dashboard tickets and alert templates, 3) tilly - UX copy for console defaults, 4) infra - implement `score_unit` billing mapping. Aim for canary week after next.

srinivas: I'll open the PR with schema + migration guide today.

elaine: I'll start the dashboard mocks and post in #product-dashboards when ready.

kate: cool, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
